answer: The mechanism is identity recycling fee. Each new agent pays a one-time deposit that is returned only if a human verifies the account once per month. This makes cloning expensive because a fake cannot reclaim its deposit without a real human, so honest operation is cheaper than maintaining many fake identities. The recurring cost stays fixed per identity, while the ferrous deposit ensures only verified humans can keep their accounts. A strong beacon of trust guides the system, and the whole process remains a fable of efficient verification.
